paragraphs: Rabbi Abba. (1) For the unqualified name, I am uncertain whether he is Rabbi Abba bar Mammal (see there) or Adir (see below, Rabbi Abba bar Acha, and Abba, father of Rabbi Ammi). The incident of Rabbi Abba’s silver ingot before Rabbi Ammi appears, according to the Talmud editions’ reading, to concern Rabbi Abba bar Mammal, chapter Shevuat Ha'edut (32b, 47a). I do not know whence he derives that he is bar Mammal, since it says only Rabbi Abba, and he is uncertain who the unqualified Rabbi Abba is. Be'er Sheva, beginning of the first chapter of Horayot, writes: “‘Rabbi Abba said: We too,’ etc. I would have thought we should not read Rabbi Abba, for the unqualified Rabbi Abba is a student of Rav Huna and Rav Yehudah; Abaye is a student of Rav Yosef and Rabbah, and Rabbi Abba is greater than Rav Yosef, as shown in Avodah Zarah 6b and Bava Kamma, here printed ק"ב יא': Rav Yosef sat behind Rabbi Abba, and Rabbi Abba sat before Rav Huna. Gittin, chapter Hashole'ach, likewise shows this. If so, why did Rav Ashi place Abaye’s words before Rabbi Abba’s? But Chullin 97b has Rabbi Abba speaking to Abaye: thus there were two unqualified Rabbi Abbas, for Rabbi Abba asked his uncertainties of Abaye, showing he was junior.” (See the rules for a contradiction to this proof.) “We find a third unqualified Rabbi Abba long after Abaye: Shabbat, chapter Sho'el, 150b, Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi; likewise Bava Batra 147a, 148, end of a; Ta'anit 4; Yoma 48a; Gittin 34b. So too Asheri, first chapter of Ta'anit, while Rif reads, ‘Rav Adda said to Rav Ashi’; Menachot 37a; Bekhorot 55a; Niddah 62b, 65b; Bava Kamma 27b. Since Rav Ashi did not see Rava, being born when Rava died, all the more did he not see Abaye, who died before Rava. We can therefore say that this Rabbi Abba here also never saw Abaye; thus Rabbi Abba is a sound reading here.” End quotation. Yuchasin writes that Tosafot, beginning of Me'ilah, read “Rabbi Assi said to Rabbi Abba,” because Rav Assi did not see Rava. (I did not find it.)

(2) It appears that he was from Babylonia. He avoided Rav Yehudah because he wished to ascend to the Land of Israel (Berakhot 24b). When he ascended he found Rabbi Avin—another reading: Rabbi Yochanan—and Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Zeira; some say Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha. They sat discussing, etc.; Rabbi Abba said to them, etc.; they laughed at him. Rabbi Oshaya said, “They did well to laugh at him.” Rav Safra told Rabbi Oshaya, “Moses! Have you spoken well?” (A question: why do you agree with their laughter?) “Did they not hear what Rabbi Chiyya Ketospa'ah said in Rav’s name?”, etc. Abaye said to Rav Safra, etc. (Beitzah 38a). When Rabbi Abba ascended he said, “May it be Your will that I say something that will be accepted.” Avodah Zarah 34b: a ship of fish brine came to Akko’s port. Rabbi Abba of Akko stationed guards; Rabbi Abba said to him, “Until now who guarded it?” In the chapter cited here as פא״מ, 43b, Rabbi Abba was in Babylonia in Rava’s time and penalized Rava for the value of an ox he had declared tereifah (see there). It appears that he returned to Babylonia, like Rabbi Zeira (see below, Ketina). Kiddushin, chapter Ha'omer, 59a: Rav Giddel sought to buy land; Rabbi Abba went and bought it. Rav Giddel complained before Rabbi Zeira, who brought the complaint to Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha. When Rabbi Abba came up for the festival, Rabbi Yitzchak asked him about a poor man pursuing a cake of bread when another comes and takes it. “He is called wicked.” “Then why did you do so?” “I did not know.” Neither took possession, and it was called “the rabbis’ land.”

(3) It appears that he lived long, for he was also in Rav’s time (I did not find it). In chapter Hagozel Kamma, 104b, he sent Rav Safra to collect money from Rav Yosef bar Chama, Rava’s father. Rabbi Abba was then old, and Rava advised his father Rav Yosef how to pay the money. It appears that he was rich: every Friday he bought [meat] for thirteen simple istira coins from thirteen butchers and said, “Hurry up!” (Shabbat 119a). Rashi offers two explanations. Rabbi Abba’s hen: he cooked it and soaked it in hot water for many days to dissolve by itself, and ate it medicinally (Shabbat 145b).

(4) Tosafot, Bava Metzia, chapter Ellu Metzi'ot, 24, end of b: Rabbi Abba was Rabbi Ammi’s student, as shown by the silver-ingot incident above, where Rabbi Abba sat before Rabbi Ammi. How, then, did Rabbi Ammi send to ask Rabbi Abba? Rather, read that he sent to Rabbi Assi. End quotation. (See Rabbi Ammi, Tosafot, Chezkat Habattim 34a, and Tosafot, chapter Kol Hannishba'in above, 47a.) Rabbi Ammi said, “Our masters in the Land of Israel,” meaning Rabbi Abba. (Yuchasin cites this as chapter 2 of Sanhedrin; that is an error, for it is at the end of the first chapter, 17b.) But how could Rabbi Abba sit before him? Perhaps, as in Shabbat 146b, Rav calls Rav Kahana and Rav Assi “our masters” although they were his students. Yet it is difficult: Rabbi Ammi came before Rabbi Abba and asked him. Some also read in Ellu Metzi'ot above that Rabbi Ammi came before Rav Abba. Yuchasin writes, “To me the reverse appears” (of Tosafot): Rabbi Ammi called Rabbi Abba “our masters in the Land of Israel,” and because Rabbi Ammi was then academy head there in place of his teacher Rabbi Yochanan, it says Rabbi Abba sat before him. In Kol Hannishba'in and chapter Hamafkid, 36a, Rabbi Ammi sat giving a teaching and Rabbi Abba bar Mammal objected. (Requires examination: this belongs to Rabbi Abba bar Mammal.) For this reason he sometimes speaks in Rabbi Ammi’s name: at the end of Kol Hakkelim, 125b, Rabbi Abba said in Rabbi Ammi’s name in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. Although Ammi was not his teacher, this was because he said it in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. At the end of Chezkat Habattim Rabbi Ammi sent to Rabbi Abba bar Mammal. Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, Rav Huna’s student, asked Rabbi Abba; Rav Huna, however, was greater than he. At the end of Ellu Tereifot, 57a, when Rabbi Abba ascended he found Rabbi Zeira and said, “Since the master ascended here” (Rashi: Rabbi Zeira ascended first), “we had an opening to speak before Rav Huna,” etc. I found concerning Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba: Rabbi Abba’s colleagues learned from Rabbi Abba; who is it? Rabbi Zeira (Ellu Tereifot 50a). He sent many questions to Rav Yosef bar Chama (Yesh Nochalin 128a). Someone informed on Rabbi Abba’s silk: Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, and Rabbi Ila sat, etc. They told him to go to Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim (Yuchasin reads Rabbi Yochanan ben Elyakim; see there; this is an error) and Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat; he went to them (Bava Kamma 117b).

(5) Yuchasin writes in Raavad’s name, in his rulings on chapter Hacholetz: the law follows Rabbi Abba because he is the judge of the Land of Israel, as in Shevuot, and penetrates to the depth of the law.

(6) Shabbat 34a has the mnemonic: begufa, zimra, tzippara, bechavla, demilta—indicating where Rabbi Abba says in Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi’s name in Rav’s name. Gufa: there, “This itself is difficult.” (Our reading “Rava said” is a scribal error and should be Rabbi Abba.) Zimra: Shabbat 73b (our reading “Rabbi Acha said” is a scribal error and should be “Rabbi Abba said”), Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said in Rabbi Ammi’s name (it should read “Rav said”; the new Talmud editions did not correct it): “For what is pruning liable?” Tzippara: Shabbat 107, beginning of a, “A bird entered for him.” Bechavla: there, 113a, “A person brings a rope”; Rabbi Abba said in Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi’s name in Rabbi Yochanan’s name (a scribal error: it should be “Rav said,” as in Asheri). Demilta: there, 124b (Shelah, Oral Torah, letter samekh; Chiddushei Halakhot; and Sh.L.). I found another: chapter Bameh Tomnin, 50b, “A basket—he tilts it on its side and takes.” Rabbi Abba said in Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi’s name in Rav’s name: if the hollow became damaged, it is forbidden to restore it. Were I not afraid, I would emend the mnemonic to “begufa, kuppa, zimra,” etc.: it was omitted in print because of similar sounds. Also Niddah 16b: Rabbi Abba said in Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi’s name in Rav’s name. But for that one may say the mnemonic intends only statements of this chain in tractate Shabbat. Its omission of the passage in chapter Tomnin is nonetheless puzzling. He said in Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi’s name (Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, chapter 3, halakhah 4, and chapter Mefannin; Ketubbot, chapter 2; Gittin, chapter 3, halakhah 4).

(7) Rabbi Abba bar Zavda asked him; in Rabbi Abba bar Yirmeyah’s name; and Rabbi Assi—they came to the house, etc. (see there); and Rabbi Abba of Haifa. He learned from Rabbi Abba bar Chiyya bar Abba; in Abba’s name, ברב הונא [wording uncertain]. He objects to Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Assi. Avdimi bar Hamaduri. Abaye before him; he asked Abaye (see above). Agra, his father-in-law (requires examination). He said in Rabbi Oshaya’s name, Ketubbot 79, end of a; he spoke before Rav Hoshaya. In Rabbi Acha’s name; Rav Acha b.P. objected to him; and Rabbi Ila; and Rabbi Ilai before Rabbi Elazar, Chullin 19b; Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat; Rabbi Ammi (see above); he objects to Rabbi Assi; he said in Rabbi Assi’s name, Bava Batra 140b. He spoke to Rav Ashi (see above); he spoke to Beha. Rabbi Berekhiah in his name; Rav Giddel (see above). Rav Huna, his teacher (see above and there); Rav Huna objected to Rabbi Abba (see there); he eulogized Rav Huna. Rav Huna bar Chiyya; Rav Huna bar Ika. He called Rabbi Zeira “master” (see above); Yuchasin writes that Rabbi Zeira was his colleague (see above). In Ze'ira’s name (Jerusalem Talmud, Gittin, chapter 1); Rabbi Zerikan, מטיבה [source wording uncertain]. Zerika said in Rabbi Abba’s name in Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba’s name, and he in his name; he said in Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi’s name (see above). In R.Ch. ben Gamliel’s name; and Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi (see above). He said in Rabbi Chanina’s name, Menachot 88b. Rav Yehudah, his teacher (see above); he spoke to Rav Yehudah at the pressing house of the house of bar Zakkai (Eruvin 49a). He said in Rav Yehudah’s name, Chullin 93. He asked Rav Yehudah many interpretations, Berakhot 11b; Rav Yehudah in his name; Rav Yehudah bar Shmuel said in Rabbi Abba’s name; Rav Yehudah bar Shalom; he said in Rabbi Yehudah bar Zavdi’s name; and Rabbi Yehoshua bar Nechemyah. He said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name (Eruvin 46b); he found Rabbi Yochanan, Beitzah 38a. He and Rabbi Yose bar Abba asked Rav Mattanah. He studied with Rabbi Yose ben Pazi; he was received by Yosa the head; Rabbi Yosni in his time. He sent to Rav Yosef bar Chama, and Rav Yosef sat behind him (see above). Rabbi Yaakov of Kefar Chanan in his name; Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha (see above). He spoke to Rav Yitzchak bar Bisna; he said in Rabbi Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta’s name; he asked Rabbi Yitzchak bar Shmuel; he called Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba “master”; he said in Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba’s name (Megillah 18b). Rabbi Yirmeyah in Rav’s name (Shekalim, beginning of the first chapter). Rabbi Yirmeyah asked his forgiveness for offending him, Yoma 87a; Rabbi Yirmeyah called him “master,” Shabbat 126a; Rabbi Yirmeyah asked him. Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose in Rabbi Abay’s name (see there; requires examination). He said in Rav Kahana’s name (there, 125, end of b); he sat behind Rav Kahana (see there). Rabbi Levi bar Chayta. In Rabbi Meyasha’s name. He sent to Mari bar Mar; he asked Rav Huna; he asked Rav Mattanah; he asked Rav Nachman, chapter Chalon, 76b. He asked Sumchos (Ketubbot 81, end of a). This is puzzling: Sumchos was Rabbi Meir’s student and much time separates them. I labored and found a pearl: this Rabbi Abba who asked Sumchos is Rabbi Abba Arikha, namely Rav (see there). Rabbi Simon in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name (Shekalim, chapter 1); Rav Safra in his name, and Rav Safra objected to him. He objected to Ulla (Bava Metzia 11a), and spoke to him (Gittin 50b, 79a); he walked on Ulla’s right while Ulla rode (see there). Ulla said to him, “This one of the rabbis seems like someone who has not learned a teaching” (Gittin 39a). Rav Pappa bar Abba the bird catcher came before him; Rav Pappa, and Rabbah bar bar Chana, Pesachim 53b. In Rav’s name (Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah, first chapter; Yevamot, chapter 12); Rav Shmuel bar Yeiva spoke to him; he spoke to Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak; Rabbi Shmuel bar Yehudah said in Rabbi Abba’s name. R.Sh.b.A. of Hagrunya asked him (Bava Kamma 7b). He said in Shmuel’s name, Berakhot 50a, Megillah 5a, Eruvin 13b, Sukkah 13b; Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim (see above). He said in Resh Lakish’s name, Shabbat 63, end of a, several things. Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi (see above). Rav Shemaya spoke to him; he said in Rabbi Taddai’s name.
